Summary of the null-model tests of T-statistics

Source: R/trait_variation.R
tstats_summary.Rd

Summarises the result of tstats() with null models: for each trait and statistic, the share of sites below and above the null distribution, the mean standardised effect size and a test of the mean over sites, and the sites that deviate.

Usage

tstats_summary(x, level = 0.95)

Arguments

x

Data frame from tstats() with n_perm > 0.

level

Coverage of the null distribution, as in null_intervals() and plot.tstats(): each site and the mean are tested two-sided at size \(\alpha = 1 - \mathrm{level}\). A site can deviate only if \(1 / (1 + \mathrm{n_perm}) < \alpha / 2\), so n_perm must be at least \(2 / \alpha\); a warning is given otherwise. Before 0.7.0 level was the size (0.05); values below 0.5 are still read that way, with a warning.

Value

A list with two data frames. traits has one row per trait and statistic, with the columns trait, statistic, n_sites (testable sites), percent_low, percent_high, mean_ses, p_mean_low, p_mean_high, sites_low and sites_high (site names separated by spaces). sites has one row per site, trait and statistic, with observed, ses, p_low, p_high and deviation ("low", "high", "none" or NA).

Details

Each site is tested in both directions from the null values kept by tstats(): the p-value of a low value is \((1 + r) / (1 + n)\), where \(r\) is the number of null values at or below the observed one and \(n\) the number of null values, and that of a high value counts null values at or above it. A site deviates when one of the two is below \(\mathrm{level} / 2\), so that the two tests together have size level. A site cannot be tested when its observed value is missing or when every null value equals the observed one, as for T_IP.IC at a site with one species, where the statistic is 1 whatever the permutation; such sites get NA and are left out of the shares, instead of a small p-value in both directions.

The test of the mean compares the mean of the observed statistic over the testable sites with the mean over the same sites of each randomisation, so that the null distribution of the mean keeps the dependence among sites within a randomisation.

See also

tstats().

Examples

set.seed(1)
tree <- treeshapesim::sim_tree_shape(20)
sim <- simulate_metacommunity(landscape_implicit(15), species_traits(tree),
                              competition_matrix(tree, "none"), n_steps = 100,
                              seed_steps = 1:5)
res <- tstats(sample_individuals(sim, intraspecific_sd = 2), n_perm = 99)
tstats_summary(res)$traits
#>   trait statistic n_sites percent_low percent_high    mean_ses p_mean_low
#> 1 trait   T_IP.IC      15   100.00000     0.000000 -14.3546962       0.01
#> 2 trait   T_IC.IR      15    26.66667     6.666667  -0.8778137       0.04
#> 3 trait   T_PC.PR      15     0.00000     0.000000   0.3734805       0.89
#>   p_mean_high
#> 1        1.00
#> 2        0.97
#> 3        0.12
#>                                                                                         sites_low
#> 1 site1 site2 site3 site4 site5 site6 site7 site8 site9 site10 site11 site12 site13 site14 site15
#> 2                                                                        site2 site4 site5 site12
#> 3                                                                                                
#>   sites_high
#> 1           
#> 2      site6
#> 3
